transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll keep this tight — 40 minutes ish. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Carlos (Brightline): Carlos here, Platform team. Asha is on video but muted.
[00:12] Asha (Brightline): hi all, Asha here.
[00:14] Tom (Brightline, Security): Tom here.
[00:17] Jordan: Awesome. Maya from our side?
[00:20] Maya (Redwood SE): Yup, Maya on. I'll lead the infra walkthrough after the quick status.
[00:25] Jordan: Cool. Agenda — 1) staging reachability updates, 2) KMS and credentials, 3) latency baseline, 4) blockers & next steps.
[00:34] Carlos: On reachability, we got the initial gateway route working but we saw intermittent timeouts when the token size goes up, like when Asha's batch jobs run. We still think it's a routing/NAT issue.
[00:45] Maya: Hmm, that sounds like connection reuse + NAT timeout. Are you seeing TCP resets or just requests hanging?
[00:51] Carlos: Mostly hangs, eventually 504s. The logs show the connection being torn, looks like ephemeral port exhaustion maybe.
[01:00] Jordan: That could be on the cloud side — do you have keepalive configured and connection pooling?
[01:05] Carlos: We're using the standard kube-proxy setup, nothing special. We can add keepalives.
[01:10] Maya: We recommend long-lived connections for batched inference; also our gateway has a retry policy that can help if you allow the IP ranges. We sent the allowlist earlier but maybe the egress ranges weren't added to the NAT.
[01:20] Tom: On that, I flagged a ticket with infra — looks like the NAT gateway is using a small pool. I'll expand and confirm, but we need a confirmation from Redwood on exact IP ranges.
[01:30] Jordan: I'll resend the IP range doc in the chat after the call — quick link: https://redwood.test/poc-ip-ranges (note: staging ranges, not the prod list).
[01:40] Asha: Great. On KMS — we tried pulling the test key but decryption failed. Error message references HSM policy.
[01:48] Maya: We sometimes see that when key policies need explicit usage perms for the service principal. Are you using a cloud KMS or on-prem HSM?
[01:54] Carlos: Cloud KMS (KeyVault for them, sorry I keep calling it K V vault).
[01:58] Maya: Ok, likely a policy thing. We can provide a guided policy template. I can share a terraform snippet that wires the service account to key permissions.
[02:07] Carlos: That'd be super helpful. We've been blocked there — can't rotate keys programmatically.
[02:12] Jordan: Sounds like a critical path. Maya, can you own the KMS template?
[02:16] Maya: Yep, I'll put sample terraform and also an ad-hoc script to rotate once for testing.
[02:22] Tom: We'll need to validate audit logs and key usage for compliance. Can Redwood provide at least a short log sample format?
[02:29] Maya: Yes — we can export example audit entries (sanitized). I'll attach to the thread.
[02:33] Jordan: Switching to latency — Asha, you sent us the first run from your pipeline?
[02:38] Asha: Yeah, we ran a small batch workload. p50 was roughly 140ms, p90 ~320ms, p99 spiky to ~700ms. But that p99 seems tied to cold-key loads and occasional retry storms.
[02:48] Jordan: Thanks. Our hosted baseline for the same model at similar batch size is p50 95ms, p90 210ms on the shared pool. When you hit contention we see those p99 spikes too.
[02:57] Maya: Two levers: we can enable KV-prefetch and increase the pre-warm cache window for the model; or move to a small dedicated pool which will reduce jitter but cost more.
[03:07] Carlos: Cost is a concern. We're not sure if the weekly budget supports a dedicated pool yet. What's the expected uplift in cost?
[03:12] Jordan: Rough estimate — small dedicated pool for this model would be ~3.5x the unit cost vs. shared for steady-state, but reduces p99 by up to 60% in our experience for bursty pipelines.
[03:22] Tom: From security side, can Dedicated be VPC-only and enforce customer-managed KMS?
[03:27] Maya: Yes — our Dedicated offering supports VPC peering and customer KMS integration; there are a few onboarding steps but it's supported. The private deployment is more involved but we can scope if needed.
[03:36] Asha: For next week we'd like a clear path to remove the KMS blocker and to try KV-prefetch. If that lowers p99 to <300ms, we might not need a dedicated pool.
[03:46] Jordan: Makes sense. Maya, can you schedule a short runbook walk-through for KV-prefetch and cache warm? Maybe 30 minutes?
[03:52] Maya: Yep, I can do Tuesday 11/03 10am PT.
[03:56] Carlos: That works for me.
[03:58] Tom: I'll calendar hold. On audit/compliance, we need SOC2-ready logging examples and to see retention controls. Is there an enterprise docs link?
[04:06] Jordan: I'll send the compliance pack — SOC2, ISO, data retention, and logging samples. It includes retention windows and redact options.
[04:12] Tom: Good.
[04:14] Asha: Back to benchmark — are you able to share trimmed CSVs that show raw latency distribution by request size? Our profiler needs that.
[04:22] Jordan: I'll trim and annotate the CSV and include p50/p90/p99 columns plus request-size buckets. Expect that by Monday.
[04:28] Asha: Thanks. Also, we observed a big latency delta when the prompt size grows from 256 to 1k tokens — is that expected?
[04:35] Maya: Yes, token count impacts kv cache size and attention compute — that's expected. We can help with quantization profiles and advise on max-input truncation; sometimes moving heavy context to external memory (embeddings + retrieval) helps.
[04:46] Carlos: We might try prompt engineering as a short term. For long-term, we'd like to measure cost per quality point.
[04:52] Jordan: We can run a small eval set to show tradeoffs — cost vs quality vs latency. We'll include that in the benchmark deliverable.
[04:59] Tom: On credentials, we need rotation to be audited. Will Redwood's pilot logs show key rotation events?
[05:04] Maya: We can surface rotation events in the audit log export; the sample will show a rotation event and who triggered it.
[05:11] Jordan: Any other blockers?
[05:13] Carlos: Two tickets: one is KMS policy, second is NAT egress capacity. Both are in triage.
[05:18] Jordan: Ok let's pair up on owners. Ticket 1 (KMS): Maya + Carlos. Ticket 2 (NAT): Tom + Carlos + Jordan to verify IP ranges.
[05:27] Asha: Timeline wise, if we clear KMS by 11/04 and NAT by 11/03, we can run a full 24-hour soak the following week.
[05:36] Jordan: That soak will give us better p99 signals. If p99 still >500ms after KV-prefetch, we should reconvene to scope a small dedicated pool.
[05:45] Maya: Quick note — we saw in your logs some request payloads including user PII fields. Reminder: please use field redaction in staging or opt-in encryption for those fields.
[05:55] Carlos: Yep, we'll sanitize the dataset and update the pipeline — thanks for the callout.
[06:00] Jordan: Ok let's do a quick recap.
[06:02] Maya: Recap: Maya to send terraform KMS snippet + audit sample; Jordan to send benchmark CSV + IP ranges doc + compliance pack; Carlos to provide test creds and confirm NAT pool change; Tom to confirm allowlist and retention questions.
[06:18] Priya (Brightline PM): Quick question — what's the expected decision criteria for moving to Dedicated? Is it strictly latency?
[06:24] Jordan: Primary decision levers are: p99 latency stability under realistic load, cost delta vs. business value, and compliance constraints. If you can't meet SLOs with caching and pre-warm, Dedicated is next.
[06:36] Priya: Got it. Thanks.
[06:39] Jordan: Any last items?
[06:41] Tom: Nothing else.
[06:42] Jordan: Great — we'll follow up in the thread. Thanks everyone.
